suggested_experiment_name: Gamma-ray attenuation (EBL optical depth, Fermi-LAT/IACT blazars)
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1 (plot shows log10(g_agamma/GeV^-1); values converted from log10 readings)
notes: Paper sets strongest bounds on ALP-photon coupling g_agamma over the 8-25 eV mass range using gamma-ray optical depth measurements from ~800 blazars (Fermi-LAT + Cherenkov telescopes). No numerical table of the exclusion curve is provided; results are shown in Fig. 3 (contours in the m_a vs g_agamma / Gamma_a planes). The only explicit numbers in text are the best-fit values m_a c^2 = 9.1 eV, Gamma_a = 2.5e-24 s^-1 (g_agamma = 2.1e-11 GeV^-1), with a 2.1-sigma preference for the ALP signal over null; the paper interprets the result as an upper bound. Data points above are approximate reconstructions of the upper-limit curve assuming a roughly mass-independent decay-rate limit (~1e-23 s^-1) scaled from the stated best fit via g ~ sqrt(Gamma)/m^1.5, consistent with the stated ~order-of-magnitude improvement over globular cluster bounds (~6.6e-11 GeV^-1) in this range. These values should be verified against digitized Fig. 3 contours.
